title: The lord of the beasts lets this one go

words.role: opens the relative clause; resumed by paśūnām

words.gram: present, 3rd sg. middle (Vedic ईशे for ईष्टे)

words.meaning: Paśupati, the lord of beasts (a name of Rudra)

words.context: Bhāskara: «चतुष्पदां गवादीनां», cattle and the like

words.role: joins the two kinds of beasts

words.gram: past passive participle, m. nom. sg.
words.context: Bhāskara: «निष्कृष्य परिगृहीतः», taken out and set apart

words.role: main verb of the first wish
main verb of the second wish

sandhi.rule: Vedic: the visarga before p is s (रायस्पोष is also a fixed phrase)

morphology.note: Vedic third singular middle without the -t- (ईशे for ईष्टे); Bhāskara cites P. 7.1.41 (लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेषु) for the loss of t.

translation.literal: Of which beasts Paśupati is lord, four-footed and two-footed — redeemed, may this one go to the share fit for sacrifice; may increases of wealth be the sacrificer’s.
translation.readable: This beast belongs to Paśupati, lord of all creatures with four feet and with two; now it is released from him — let it go to its place in the sacrifice, and let the sacrificer’s wealth increase.

meaning: A triṣṭubh verse of the animal sacrifice. The victim belongs to Paśupati, the lord of beasts — Rudra — as do all creatures with four feet or two; the verse ‘buys it off’ from him so that it may pass to the gods’ share, and prays that the sacrificer’s wealth in cattle may grow. In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (3.1.4.1) it belongs to the mantras for leading up the victim (Bhāskara calls it the second of the series). The use of the verse for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition, not to the Veda: in its source it serves another rite (see the commentary).
in_the_rite: The third mantra of Sūrya’s step in the Navagraha sūktam, naming Paśupati (Rudra). S names the adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together in the salutation that follows, without saying which mantra is whose.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara: «येषां पशूनामीशे ईष्टे पशुपतिः», «चतुष्पदां गवादीनां उत च अपि च द्विपदां मनुष्यादीनां च येषामीष्टे»; the victim, «निष्कृष्य परिगृहीतः», goes to the sacrificial share — «यज्ञभागतां प्रतिपद्यताम्» — and the prayer for wealth asks that the cattle not leave the sacrificer: «माऽपक्रमिषुः अस्मात्पशवः».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Metre triṣṭubh (Bhāskara: «अथ द्वितीया - येषामिति त्रिष्टुप्»). Not in the Ṛgveda.
